Optimize applies `update_persisted_segment_meta(output)` (`collection.cc:863–867`), `apply` + `flush` the version again (`collection.cc:872–877`), and returns OK (`collection.cc:914`).\n6. **Reopen**: `recovery()` opens W read-only; no writing block → `recover()` never runs; `load_persist_scalar_blocks` finds no SCALAR blocks → `doc_ids_` empty (`segment.cc:3913–3959`). Doc count 0; the recovered documents are gone despite the WAL bytes still lying on disk.\n\nControl case: without the crash, `append_wal()` kept `wal_file_` open with records, so step 2's `flush()` ran fully (persist files + meta conversion + version update), and only then removed the WAL (`segment.cc:2304–2315`) — promotion referenced real files.\n\nCorroborating inconsistency (source-level, not executed): if other persisted segments exist, the `CompactTask` path scans inputs (`segment_helper.cc:233`), and `scan()` on the promoted-but-unflushed W would dereference the removed optional at `segment.cc:2837` (`std::bad_optional_access`) — the promoted state is internally invalid either way.\n\n## 3. Why \"success\" and same-handle statistics prove nothing here\n\n- Every status in the chain is manufactured without touching W's data: `flush()` early-returns OK (`segment.cc:2219–2221`); `dump()`, `switch_to_new_segment_for_writing`, the index task, and `Optimize` merely propagate it. `version_manager_->flush()` only serializes the manifest protobuf (`version_manager.cc:76–115, 282`); nothing validates that a segment added to `persisted_segment_metas` has any persisted blocks or backing files.\n- `Stats()` sums `segment->doc_count()` over the **live in-memory handles** (`collection.cc:403–441` → `doc_ids_.size()`, `segment.cc:589–600`); fetch/scan serve from `memory_store_` (`segment.cc:2825–2842`); `reload_vector_index` (`segment.cc:1882+`) swaps only vector indexers. So the same handle keeps reporting N docs from the very RAM copy that was never persisted, while the on-disk manifest already describes a world without them. The divergence is observable only by reopening — or by comparing manifest vs. files.\n- Side effect (inferred from the RocksDB-backed `IDMap`, `src/db/index/common/id_map.cc:36–42`, not execution-verified): replay re-upserts pk→doc-id entries, so after reopen the id map can still reference doc ids no segment contains.\n\n## 4. Smallest repair principle and a regression test (described, not implemented)\n\n**Principle:** \"Is there unpersisted data?\" must be answered from durable/write state (rows in the writing block / WAL contents on disk), never from whether *this process* happens to hold an open WAL handle; and a WAL may become unreachable only *after* the rows it covers are in files referenced by a committed manifest.\n\n**Smallest repair:** at the end of `SegmentImpl::recover()` (or in the recovery branch of `Open`, `segment.cc:498–501`), when records were replayed, attach the member handle by calling the existing `open_wal_file()` (`segment.cc:4303–4322`; it opens the existing file and seeks to end). Then `has_record()` is true (file-size based), and the first `flush()` — from `dump()` in Optimize, from `close()` (`segment.cc:552`), or from rollover (`segment.cc:841–844`) — runs the full persist path and removes the WAL only after `update_version()`. No change to `flush()` itself. (Equivalent alternative: widen the guard at `segment.cc:2219` to treat `memory_store_` rows / writing-block `doc_count_ > 0` as dirty. Defense in depth: refuse promotion in `switch_to_new_segment_for_writing` when the meta would be persisted with `doc_count() > 0` but zero SCALAR blocks.)\n\n**Regression test** — fits the existing `tests/db/crash_recovery` harness (fork + SIGKILL, `data_generator.cc`, `utility.h`). Note the existing `CrashDuringOptimize` (`tests/db/crash_recovery/optimize_recovery_test.cc:144`) misses this because the writer is closed cleanly first (close → flush, `segment.cc:552`) and after crash-reopen it *inserts new docs* (re-opening `wal_file_`) before optimizing:\n\n1. Child A: create collection, insert N docs (N small enough to stay under `max_buffer_size_` rollover), then SIGKILL/`_exit` — no Close, no Flush.\n2. Process B: `Collection::Open`; assert `Stats().doc_count == N` and `Fetch` returns all N (passes today; guards replay itself).\n3. Same B, **no inserts**: `Optimize()` returns OK; `Stats().doc_count == N`.\n4. End B (two variants: clean Close, and SIGKILL — durability must hold for both).\n5. Process C: `Collection::Open`; assert `Stats().doc_count == N`, fetch every pk and compare full contents, run a top-k vector query. **This assertion fails on current source** (C sees 0).\n6. Optional structural invariant (diagnostic rather than count-based): after step 3, no `*.wal` may exist under any segment directory listed as persisted in the current manifest, and every persisted segment meta must have ≥1 SCALAR block whose forward file exists with matching doc count.\n\n**Established vs. needs-execution:** the entire causal chain (null `wal_file_` → no-op flush → promotion with empty meta → manifest flush → WAL never replayed again) is traceable statically end-to-end for the FLAT/default-index single-segment case.
